questions.q: Which find option restricts matches to directories only?
questions.explain: -type d restricts results to directories; -type f restricts them to regular files.

options: Files created in the last 30 minutes
Files whose content was last modified more than 30 days ago
questions.explain: -mtime +30 matches files whose modification time is older than 30 days — useful for finding stale files to clean up.

options: A placeholder for the current matched filename
questions.explain: {} is substituted with the current file find has matched, letting -exec run a command against each result individually.

questions.q: Why would you pipe find's output into xargs rather than using -exec for a very large number of matching files?
options: xargs can search subdirectories that -exec cannot
xargs batches many filenames into fewer command invocations, which is typically faster at scale
-exec cannot delete files, only xargs can
xargs is required whenever more than one file matches
questions.explain: xargs groups multiple filenames into a smaller number of command invocations instead of launching one process per file, which is more efficient on large result sets.

questions.q: What does `xargs -I{}` let you do that plain xargs does not?
options: Place the placeholder anywhere in the command, not just at the end
Search by file size instead of name
questions.explain: -I{} defines a placeholder you can position anywhere in the command, such as `ssh {} uptime`, instead of xargs always appending arguments at the end.
